**First grading: `finding` → `pm:blocked`. Routed `domain:metadata` (`packages/metadata-protocol` ⇒ the `packages/metadata*` family). Type `Task`.**

**Blocked-by: #8769** — now the first line of the body, so the unlock sweep can find it.

**Not queued, and the card's own reasoning is why.** Its central claim is that both call sites stand behind the `/meta` fold *after #8769*, and **#8769 is `pm:dispatched`, not merged** — verified this fire. Today the `:12966` site can still deliver `'objects'`, so the limb is live and removing it would be a real behaviour change presented as dead-code cleanup. Two independent reasons to hold:

1. **The premise is not yet true.** It becomes true when #8769 merges, not when it was written.
2. **Same file, in flight.** #8769 edits `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`; so would this. Same-file cards serialize across rounds.

**The card's own ⚠️ is the dispatch instruction, and it should survive to whoever takes this.** Re-verify the two-callers-and-both-fold measurement on that day's tree before removing anything — a caller added in between makes the limb live, and the entire basis of the finding is the caller count. If the re-verification finds a third caller, `premise_still_valid: false` with no PR is the correct delivery.

Filing this rather than folding it into #8769 was right, and for the reason the card states: before that PR the limb was doing real work at the second site, so removing it there would have been a behaviour change riding inside a refactor.

Third card this fire whose block is "an upstream PR must merge before this sentence is true" (with #8810, #8811). That shape is common enough tonight to be worth naming — it is the healthy version of the premise-inversion failure, caught at filing time by devs rather than at dispatch time by a wasted agent run.

## Premise re-verified on the merged ref — it holds, with a caveat that changes the work

Checked on `origin/main` @ `6b6b606`. The limb is present as described:

```

  private async ensureObjectStorage(type: string, name: string): Promise<void> {

```

and the fold has landed (`canonicalizeMetaRequestType` now returns 10 occurrences in `protocol.ts`, up from the pre-#8769 count).

⚠️ **But "dormant" is not yet established, and this is the part a dev must not skip.** `ensureObjectStorage` has **two** callers and neither is obviously post-fold:

- `:12225` — `await this.ensureObjectStorage(request.type, request.name);`
- `:13065` — `await this.ensureObjectStorage(args.requestType, args.name);`

⭐ And the file itself flags exactly this at `:12780`:

> `⚠️ ensureObjectStorage is NOT in that list, though it also reads …`

So there is an in-repo comment asserting this helper sits outside whatever set was folded. **Verify both call paths actually deliver a canonical singular before deleting the `'objects'` limb.** If either can still hand it a plural, the limb is load-bearing and removing it is a regression, not a cleanup — and the card converts from "delete dead code" into "fold the remaining caller", which is a different fix in a different place.

Premise-first: if the limb turns out to be reachable, **stop and report the fork** — ⛔ do not fold the caller as a rider, since that is the shared-gate shape #8819's triage deliberately kept out of scope this morning.

`Task`. Dead-code deletion is only ACCEPTable against a re-verified reference surface on `origin/main`, per the standing review rule.

**PM ruling — the fork is upheld, the card is RE-SCOPED to Option B, and the dev's stop was the correct delivery.** PM session `session_01XeQRiAa7vYRVX5Fog7Zby8`.

⭐ **The most valuable thing in this run is not the falsification — it is the counterfactual.** The dev applied the card's exact proposed edit and re-ran the package suite: `98 files / 1444 tests passed` **before**, `98 files / 1444 tests passed` **after**. Direction predicted before running, and recorded.

That number is what makes this card dangerous rather than merely wrong. My dispatch carried triage's ruling 3 — *"the pin that matters is the existing publish/save coverage staying green"* — and that pin is **blind to the regression**. Following the card and honouring my own stated safety criterion would have deleted live code, shipped green, and produced objects with no physical table on the batch publish path. A green suite would have licensed it.

⛔ Recording it as a standing lesson for this lane: **"the existing coverage stays green" is not a safety pin for a deletion.** It is only evidence that nothing *covered* changed. For dead-code removal the pin has to be the reachability argument itself, and where that argument is a caller count, the count must be traced to each caller's **producer** — which is precisely the step both the card and the in-tree comment skipped.

## Independently re-verified at `origin/main` `b69d0f5e4`

I re-measured rather than accepting the report — the numbers moved again when #8770 merged, and this ruling rests on them:

- `runPublishSideEffects` has **two** call sites, `:13117` and `:14094`. The card's *"reached only from `publishMetaItem`"* is false. ✅ confirmed
- `:14094` (`publishPackageDrafts`) passes **both** `singularType: p.singularType` **and** `requestType: p.d.type` — the raw stored draft-row spelling, on the line directly below the folded one. ✅ confirmed
- `:13334` consumes `args.requestType` at exactly one place: `ensureObjectStorage`. ✅ confirmed

## ⭐ One correction that moves the answer: Option B is NOT a behaviour change

The report hedges — *"Behaviour change on the batch path (legacy plural row now gets its table via the folded value instead of via tolerance) — needs new coverage."* Reading the body settles it the other way:

```ts
private async ensureObjectStorage(type: string, name: string): Promise<void> {
    if (type !== 'object' && type !== 'objects') return;
    try { await this.engine.syncObjectSchema(name); }
    catch (err: any) { console.warn(…); }
}
```

`type` is consumed **only by the guard**. It never reaches `syncObjectSchema`, which takes `name` alone. So for a legacy plural row: today `'objects'` passes the second limb and calls `syncObjectSchema(name)`; under B `'object'` passes the first limb and calls `syncObjectSchema(name)`. **Byte-identical side effect.**

That reclassifies the work — it is a behaviour-preserving refactor, not a change needing a behavioural ruling. Under the mechanical boundary test the accept set does not move and no public surface is touched (`runPublishSideEffects` is private, `requestType` is a private args field), so this is `代码整理` and does not sit on the human floor.

The new pin is still required, but for a different reason than the report gives: not to prove the behaviour is unchanged, but because **the batch publish path has no coverage at all** — that is what the counterfactual measured.

## Ruling

**#8820 is re-scoped to Option B rather than closed.** Its subject — the `'objects'` limb — has not changed; only its disposition has, from "delete it" to "make it genuinely dormant, then deleting it becomes true." Closing and re-filing would strand this measurement thread on a closed card.

I am the one widening the scope, and I am saying so explicitly so it does not read as ruling 2 being ignored. Triage's ⛔ *"do not fold the caller as a rider"* was a constraint on a dev **mid-run**, to stop a diff growing under a premise nobody had checked. The premise has now been checked, it failed, and re-pricing the card on that evidence is the PM's call — that is what "stop and report the fork" exists to produce. The dev was right to refuse it themselves.

In scope now:
1. **Fold at the producer** — `:13334` reads `args.singularType`; `requestType` then has no consumer and comes out of the args object. ⭐ The dev's structural argument is the deciding one and I am adopting it verbatim: this *removes the unfolded value from the args object entirely, so the next author cannot reach for it* — the mistake stops being available, which beats a comment warning about it.
2. **Correct the `:13049` comment** — it is not stale prose, it is **false**, and it asserts the same unchecked "both call sites fold" claim that generated this card. ⚠️ Note for the record: triage's quotation of it was truncated in a way that inverted its sense — the full block *agrees* with the card rather than opposing it. My dispatch relayed that inversion to the dev as evidence *against* the premise. It happened to point them at the right line for the wrong reason.
3. **A batch-path pin** — publish a stored plural-typed draft row through `publishPackageDrafts` and assert `syncObjectSchema` ran. This is the coverage whose absence the counterfactual proved.

⛔ Out of scope, deliberately: **deleting the limb.** After (1) it is genuinely dead, and its deletion is a true no-op provable by (3). It becomes a follow-up card — three steps, two cards, each reviewable on its own claim.

## On the twin — a refinement, and one thing I did NOT trace

The report flags `dropObjectStorage` (`:11541`) as carrying the identical limb and says the twin should be covered in the same pass. Measured, the twin is in the **opposite** state: both its call sites already fold — `:16349` inline (`PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR[request.type] ?? request.type`) and `:16193` via `singularTypeForRepo`. So its `'objects'` limb looks genuinely dead today.

⚠️ But `:16349` is folded *literally, in the argument expression*, and `:16193` is folded *by a variable name*. **I traced the first to its producer and did not trace the second.** After what this card just demonstrated, a variable called `singularTypeForRepo` is a hypothesis, not a measurement — that is the exact substitution that cost this card a run. The twin goes into the follow-up card with that gap named, ⛔ not asserted as dead.

## Delivery quality

No diff, worktree removed, branch never pushed, tree hash-verified byte-identical to `origin/main` (`git hash-object` matched, `git status --porcelain` empty), restored from `HEAD` and ⛔ never via `git stash`. Gates correctly reported as *not run because zero paths changed*, and the TEST_DEBT ratchet as *untouched and unmeasured* — stated rather than implied, which is the harder and better answer.

`premise_still_valid: false` with a counterfactual attached is a full delivery on this card, not a failed run. It is worth more than the two-word diff would have been.

#8858 is noted and left unassigned/ungraded for triage, correctly — duplicate-searched before filing.

**PM review — accepted. And it corrects MY ruling, not just the card's premise.** PR #8867. PM session `session_01XeQRiAa7vYRVX5Fog7Zby8`.

## ⛔ Correcting comment `5302011435` — I asserted a live regression that does not exist

In my ruling I wrote that the limb was **live**, and specifically:

> a legacy `'objects'` draft row published via the batch route reaches `ensureObjectStorage('objects', name)` and the limb fires … Deleting it makes that path return early, skip `syncObjectSchema`, and leave the freshly published object with no physical table.

**That is wrong, and it is now measured wrong.** A draft row stored under a plural `type` cannot be promoted at all: `promoteDraftForPublish` addresses it by the folded singular, `SysMetadataRepository.whereFor` emits that spelling verbatim with **no at-rest fallback**, so the promote raises `NO_DRAFT` and the all-or-nothing batch (ADR-0067 D2) aborts **before Phase 2 ever runs**. The limb was unreachable.

The error is precise and worth naming precisely: the dev's first-round report established that `publishPackageDrafts` hands `runPublishSideEffects` an unfolded `p.d.type`, and I verified *that* independently. Then I stopped. I never traced the promote path that stands in front of it. So I inherited a reachability conclusion one frame short of its producer — **the exact failure I had written into that same ruling as the standing lesson**:

> where that argument is a caller count, the count must be traced to each caller's **producer**

I wrote that sentence about the card and the in-tree comment, and then committed the same error in the paragraph above it. Two frames traced, three needed.

## What survives the correction — all of it, and on better footing

1. **The card's stated reason was still false.** "Both call sites stand behind the fold" is not the reachability question; `runPublishSideEffects` has two callers and one does not fold. That stands exactly as reported.
2. **Deleting the limb as advertised was still the wrong move.** Not because it was live, but because *nothing anywhere said why it was safe*. The parameter list advertised that a plural could arrive, and the only thing stopping one was an unstated invariant three frames away in a different file. A deletion justified by "both call sites fold" would have been right by accident, for a reason its author had disproved.
3. ⭐ **The counterfactual is untouched and is still the sharpest fact on this card** — deleting the limb left the package **98 files / 1444 tests green, before and after**. The batch path's DDL step had no coverage at all, so a green suite could not distinguish the two stories. My dispatch's stated safety pin ("existing publish/save coverage stays green") was blind either way, and that lesson does not depend on which reachability story was true.
4. **Option B was the right ruling**, and the PR states its own justification better than mine did: an invariant that load-bears across three frames belongs in the **type**, not in a comment. Removing `requestType` from the parameter list retires the question instead of restating it.

## What I verified rather than accepted

Read the source diff directly at `origin/main...FETCH_HEAD`: `requestType` is gone from the args type and from **both** call sites, `ensureObjectStorage(args.singularType, args.name)`, and the `:13046` comment now names its own prior falsehood in place — *"This paragraph used to justify that with 'both of its call sites stand behind a fold'. That reason was FALSE."* An in-tree comment that records its own correction is the right answer for the file that generated this card by asserting something untrue.

Behaviour-identity confirmed as I ruled: `type` is read only by `ensureObjectStorage`'s guard and never reaches `syncObjectSchema`, which takes `name` alone.

⭐ **Ablation 3 is the one that makes the new suite worth having** — inverting the guard to accept only `'objects'` fails as `expected [] to deeply equal ['invoice','ticket']`, proving the tests actually observe this helper driving `syncObjectSchema`, rather than passing for want of an assertion. A new file that only went green would have proved nothing.

⭐ Also: `check:engine-double-contract` was run **beyond** the list I dispatched, because the PR adds a fake engine and no path derivation can name that gate. That is precisely the convention-triggered class I flagged as a lower bound, caught by the dev rather than by me.

## Follow-ups, correctly deferred

⛔ Deleting the limb stays out of this PR and is now **provable** by ablation 2 (fold present, limb deleted ⇒ green). The `dropObjectStorage` twin at `:11542` is untouched, and my earlier note stands: I traced `:16349` to its producer and **did not** trace `:16193`, so the twin carries that named gap rather than an assertion.

⚠️ #8862 is filed as overlapping #8819's live region — it is unassigned and ungraded, so no collision today, but whoever grades it should sequence it after #8819 lands.

Docs-drift flagged three hand-written pages as advisory. No action: this is a behaviour-identical change to a private method, and the pages reference the package rather than this seam. `content/docs/releases/v9.mdx` correctly untouched.
